title: Validate constraint glob patterns at parse time — typo'd glob makes constraint silently inert
description:
crate_matches and path_matches in constraints/external.rs use Pattern::new(p).ok() — an invalid glob (e.g. unclosed bracket "foo[") compiles to None and the pattern simply never matches. For forbidden_external/confined_external this means a typo'd `crates`/`from`/`allowed_in` entry silently disables the constraint — worst possible failure mode for legally load-bearing rules like the AGPL boundary ("nothing links Arjuna").

Fix: compile all glob fields in RawConstraint::into_constraint (rules.rs) and return a ConstraintParseError on invalid patterns, so the error surfaces through the existing parse_errors channel (blocking findings). Audit whether the pre-existing kinds (forbidden_dep from/to, boundary) have the same silent-inertness via the resolver and cover them in the same pass.

Found by vidhi-review of sutra/needs-designing/14.
execution_record: Single-file change to src/rules.rs as planned. Added validate_glob and validate_crate_glob helpers that compile patterns at parse time in RawConstraint::into_constraint(), returning Err on invalid patterns. Also added validation to the old-format forbidden_deps loop in all_constraints(). Crate glob validation normalizes hyphens to underscores before compiling, matching external.rs::normalize_crate(). 9 new tests covering all glob-bearing variants plus old-format path. Downstream .ok() sites left as defense-in-depth — they're now unreachable for invalid patterns.
root_cause: Glob pattern fields in constraint kinds were compiled with Pattern::new(p).ok() at match time across 7 call sites. An invalid glob (e.g. unclosed bracket) compiles to None, causing the pattern to silently never match — making the entire constraint inert. No validation existed at parse time to catch malformed patterns.
